title: Private Deployments VPC Blueprint and Automated Evidence Checklist
summary: Operational blueprint for private deployment network hardening: recommended VPC patterns, compact firewall rule sets, mTLS zoning guidance, RBAC v2 mapping for service-to-service access, canonical audit log schema and SIEM export fields, plus an automated evidence collection checklist for compliance reviews.
body:
Purpose:
This doc is a pragmatic blueprint for teams deploying Redwood Private in customer VPCs or on-prem equivalents. The emphasis is on a minimal, reviewable surface for audits: deterministic firewall rules, strong mTLS boundaries, RBAC mappings for infra components, and a small set of canonical audit fields that our evidence automation can reliably collect and push to SIEM.

Design goals (prioritized):
- Least-privilege network paths that are small and testable.
- Deterministic, label-driven mTLS zones for service authentication and telemetry.
- RBAC v2 role sets that map to operational tasks (deploy, rollback, debug, read-only).
- Audit logs with stable, typed fields to reduce SIEM parsing work.
- A lightweight evidence automation runbook that produces a checklist plus diffs for change control.

1) High-level VPC topology (recommended pattern)
- Control VPC (optional for large orgs): central logging, CI runners, bastion proxies.
- Tenant VPC (customer private deployment): subnets for ingress, control-plane, compute (GPU pools), and management.
- Transit / Peering: keep dedicated peering/transit for management traffic; do not allow broad CIDR overlaps.

ASCII diagram (annotated):

  [Internet / Customer VPN]
          |
       IGW/NAT
          |
  --------------------------
  |   Tenant VPC (10.40.0.0/16)  |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  |  Public/Ingress Subnet  | |
  |  |  (10.40.10.0/24)        | |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  |  Control-plane Subnet   | |
  |  |  (10.40.20.0/24)        | |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  |  GPU/Serving Subnet     | |
  |  |  (10.40.30.0/24)        | |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  --------------------------  |
  |  |  Management Subnet      | |
  |  |  (10.40.40.0/24)        | |
  |  --------------------------  |
  ------------------------------

Notes:
- Each subnet gets its own route table; no cross-subnet implicit access.
- Use security groups for pod-to-pod access, and network ACLs for coarse egress controls.

2) mTLS zoning and service authentication (recommendation)
- Goal: authenticate and authorize every service-to-service TCP/TLS channel with mTLS using short-lived certs.
- Zones: Ingress -> Frontend -> Router -> Model-Serving -> Metrics/Exporter -> Control-plane.
- Each zone uses a distinct workload identity (k8s service account or VM identity).
- Certificate issuance: short TTL (1h) from local CA with automated rotation.
- Reject fallback to plaintext; require client cert validation in the TLS handshake.

Policy snippet (plain language):
- All connections from Router to Model-Serving require client cert with SAN containing: service:router, env:prod, pod:router-*.
- Model-Serving will only accept requests if ACL includes specific route_id and caller_role in RBAC audit.

3) Compact firewall rule set (examples)
- Principles: explicit allow list, single-purpose rules, no CIDR wide opens except IGW for ingress.
- Keep egress rules explicit for control-plane endpoints (upstream patching endpoints, metrics collector).

Minimum allow rules (tenant VPC):
- Ingress Subnet -> Frontend: TCP 443 from customer VPN/peer CIDRs only.
- Frontend -> Router (subnet): TCP 443 with mTLS, allow only from Frontend SG.
- Router -> Model-Serving (subnet): TCP 443 mTLS, allow only from Router SG, port-range 1024-65535 for runtime channels if using ephemeral ports.
- Model-Serving -> Control-plane (management subnet): TCP 22/443 for admin, restricted to management SG and management CIDR.
- Model-Serving -> Metrics Exporter: TCP 9100/9273 from model SG only.
- Egress: All subnets allowed to contact Redwood central logging endpoints on TCP 443 (TLS) to known IP set; block everything else by default.

Sample security group naming conventions: SG-front-prod-ingress, SG-router-prod, SG-serving-prod, SG-mgmt-prod.

4) RBAC v2 mapping (service and operator roles)
- Role families (high level):
  - infra.admin: full infra actions (create/delete subnets, modify SGs) - reserved for infra SREs.
  - infra.operator: deploy/scale/restart serving components, view logs.
  - infra.auditor: read-only view on configs and audit logs.
  - infra-service: machine-role used by control-plane components (non-human).

Example RBAC rule (plain):
- infra.operator can POST /deployments/* and PATCH /routes/* but cannot mutate VPC-level SGs or route tables.
- infra-service may call /kv/store and /kms/decrypt within the management subnet only.

Mapping to network zones: combine network SG restrictions with RBAC decisions: e.g., HTTP header caller-role enforced by service auth layer + mTLS identity ensures both network and application-level checks.

5) Canonical audit log schema (single-line JSON string per event)
- Rationale: SIEM parsers prefer stable, small set of typed fields. Keep schema compact.

Canonical fields (string or ISO timestamp):
- event_id: stable-uuid
- ts: 2026-02-20T15:04:05Z
- actor: "user:alice@redwood.ai" or "svc:router-prod"
- actor_roles: ["infra.operator"]  -- represent as bracketed string in a single-line log
- action: "network.securitygroup.update"
- resource_type: "security_group"
- resource_id: "sg-0a12b3c4"
- outcome: "success" | "failure"
- src_ip: client IP (if applicable)
- dst_ip: destination IP
- request_id: short-trace-id
- reason: optional free text for failures

Example line (as log):
{event_id: "e3b0c", ts: "2026-02-20T15:04:05Z", actor: "svc:ci-runner", actor_roles: "[infra.operator]", action: "deployment.create", resource_type: "deployment", resource_id: "rdw-deploy-17", outcome: "success", src_ip: "10.40.2.5", dst_ip: "10.40.30.12", request_id: "req-9012"}

Note: the automation agent will transform bracketed role lists into array fields for the SIEM on ingest.

6) SIEM export field mapping (recommended minimal map)
- siem.event_id -> event_id
- siem.timestamp -> ts
- siem.actor -> actor
- siem.actor_role -> actor_roles (explode bracketed list)
- siem.action -> action
- siem.resource -> resource_type/resource_id concatenated
- siem.outcome -> outcome
- network.src_ip -> src_ip
- network.dst_ip -> dst_ip
- trace.request_id -> request_id

Parsing tips: avoid free-form nested JSON in message field; duplicate key-value pairs in dedicated columns to reduce heuristics.

7) Evidence automation runbook (step-by-step)
- Goal: produce a verifiable artifact bundle for every change window or quarterly review: configs, signed certificate snapshots, ephemeral cert rotation proof, network ACL diffs, SG diffs, RBAC policy snapshot, and SIEM sample exports.
- Generated artifact list (automated):
  1) git-diff of infra repo for commits touching /private-deployments/** (signed by CI).
  2) current SG listing (describe-instances style) and a one-line digest (sha256) of the serialized SG JSON.
  3) current NACLs and route table entries + digest.
  4) mTLS cert inventory snapshot: list of active cert serials, issued_at, expires_at, subject (service id).
  5) RBAC v2 policy snapshot (compact YAML) and digest.
  6) Audit log sample export (24h) with schema-validated lines and a count per outcome.
  7) SIEM ingest proof record (timestamped event with request_id referencing the export job).

Automation details:
- The evidence agent runs as a cronjob in the management subnet with minimal read-only IAM.
- All artifacts are signed with the infra CI key and uploaded to an immutable artifacts bucket with object-locking enabled for retention.
- A change ID (e.g., PD-2345-20260220-rc1) ties all artifacts and the SIEM ingest proof.

8) Minimal compliance checklist (for auditors)
- [ ] VPC subnets documented and CIDRs approved.
- [ ] Security groups and NACLs exported and digests match last approved commit.
- [ ] mTLS enabled on all east-west ports; cert inventory shows no expired certs.
- [ ] RBAC snapshot present and no users in infra.admin aside from SRE leads.
- [ ] Audit logs collected and sample contains event_id, ts, actor, action, outcome.
- [ ] SIEM received and parsed the sample export (check SIEM ingest proof).
- [ ] Evidence bundle signed and stored in immutable bucket; object-lock metadata present.

9) Operational tests (quick commands)
- Verify SGs: run infra-cli sg export --vpc 10.40.0.0/16 | sha256sum -> compare to artifacts digest.
- mTLS smoke: curl --cert client.pem --key client.key https://10.40.30.12:443/health ; expect 200 and audit event deployment.health_check with actor svc:test-health.
- Audit sample: audit-cli tail --since 1h --filter action=deployment.create | head -n 5

Open questions / decisions pending:
- TTL for role-bound certs (1h vs 6h) — tradeoff between rotation load and compromise window.
- Standardized request_id length and entropy requirements — affects SIEM correlation performance.
- Should infra.operator be split into deploy-only and debug-only roles? (proposal: split for principle of least privilege).

Appendix A: Short checklist for on-call quickly verifying prod network after an incident
- Are all subnets healthy? infra-cli subnet status --vpc 10.40.0.0/16
- Any unexpected SG changes in the last 1h? infra-cli sg changes --since 1h
- Last cert rotation time: cert-inv last-rotate --service router-prod
- Last audit export job status: evidence-agent status --last-job

Contributors: Marcus Lee (network patterns), Diego Alvarez (SIEM mapping), Priya Kapoor (mTLS cert flow), Samantha Cho (RBAC and automation).

This is a working blueprint: expect tweaks after the first automated evidence run. If you copy parts into Confluence, keep this file as the canonical working artifact for the eng-private-deployments team.
